title: Website Design for Contractors | Vestis Solutions
description: Website design for contractors, built to be found on Google and AI search to turn visitors into calls and quote requests. You own the site and accounts.
h1: Website design for contractors, built to bring in calls
intro: Your website looks fine, but it does not bring in work. Visitors land, scroll and leave without calling. Or the site was built by someone who is gone now, and you cannot even log in to change your hours. Good website design for contractors starts with one question: does it make the phone ring?
definition: A contractor website built for leads is a site set up so local customers can find it on Google and in AI answers, understand what you do in seconds, and call or request a quote without hunting for how.

sections.h2: What makes good website design for contractors
paras: Pretty is nice. Useful pays the bills. A site that works for a contractor does a few plain things well.
bullets: Your phone number and a quote button are easy to find on every page, on a phone.
One page for each service you want more of, and for the areas you serve.
Real photos of your work and your crew, not stock images.
Reviews and proof that you are licensed and insured, where people can see them.
Fast load times and clean setup so Google and AI tools can read it.
A short quote form that goes straight to the right person, not into a forgotten inbox.

paras: A website nobody finds is a brochure in a drawer. I set up your site for Google search, Google Maps and AI answers from ChatGPT and Gemini, then keep working on it every month as part of ongoing SEO and AEO.
That means clear service pages, plain answers to the questions customers ask, and information that matches your Google Business Profile.

sections.h2: Built to turn visitors into jobs
paras: Traffic is only half of it. I look at what happens after someone fills out your form or calls. Who gets the lead, how fast do they respond, and what happens if no one answers? A good site sends leads into the tools you already use, like your CRM or scheduling software, so nothing gets lost.

sections.h2: You own the site and the accounts
paras: Your website, domain, hosting and Google accounts are in your name. If we ever stop working together, everything stays with you. No hostage situations, no surprise transfer fees.

A new site, or a rebuild of the one you have, is included in the partnership. Partnerships start at $3,000 a month for the first 90 days, then month to month. I am based in Charlotte, NC, and build sites for contractors across the US.

signs: You get website visits but very few calls or quote requests.
You cannot log in to your own website or do not know who hosts it.
Your site lists every service on one page.
It is hard to find your phone number on a phone.
Form submissions go to an inbox nobody checks.

faq.q: How much does website design for contractors cost?
faq.a: Costs range widely, from a few hundred dollars for a template to many thousands for a custom build. With Vestis, a new site or a rebuild is included in the partnership, which starts at $3,000 a month. That also covers ongoing SEO and AEO, a sales process review and owner working sessions.

faq.q: What should a contractor website include?
faq.a: A contractor website should make it easy to find you, trust you and contact you. That means a page for each main service, the areas you serve, real project photos, reviews, proof of license and insurance, and a phone number and quote form that are easy to use on a phone.

faq.q: Who owns my website if I stop working with you?
faq.a: You do. Your domain, hosting, website and Google accounts are set up in your name from the start. If the partnership ends, you keep everything and can hand it to anyone you like. Check any contract with your attorney, but ownership should always sit with the business owner.

faq.q: Should I rebuild my website or fix the one I have?
faq.a: It depends on what you have now. If your site is reasonably fast, you can log in, and it has a clear structure, fixing it is often enough. If it is slow, hard to edit or built on a platform you do not control, a rebuild usually costs less in the long run.

faq.q: Why is my contractor website not getting calls?
faq.a: Usually it is either not being found, or visitors cannot quickly see why to call you. Common causes are one page for every service, no reviews on the site, a phone number that is hard to tap on a phone, and slow load times. Each of these can be fixed.

faq.q: Will a new website help me show up in ChatGPT?
faq.a: A well-built site helps, but it is not the only factor. AI tools look at your website, reviews and business listings together. Clear service pages with plain answers give them something to quote, and matching information across the web makes your business easier to trust. No one can guarantee a mention.
